about: TRAP CASES (2026-10-03). Events and pages that have already fooled us, kept as data. Every research method (a grounded prompt, a cheap model reading a page, a rule) is scored on these before it is trusted, and the code we already run is tested against the ones it can check offline (tests/test_trap_cases.py). `fixture` is text we actually read on the live page on `read_on`; `wrong` is what a method returned or could return; `right` is the answer a person confirmed. `checks` are offline assertions against our code; a case with only `human` checks needs a person or a model to answer (the runner lists it). `gap: true` means our current code does NOT catch it: the assertion records the gap so it is not forgotten.

cases.name: The page now shows NEXT year's edition (wrong-year answer)
cases.went_wrong: Research returned a 2026 start date (2026-06-09) for the 2026 edition from a page whose title and dates are the 2027 edition.
cases.fixture: Hydrogen and Carbon Capture Technology Expo MENA 2027. The conference takes place 8-9 June 2027, ADNEC Centre, Abu Dhabi. Also on this site: 20/21/22 October 2026 and 10/11 February 2027 (other events of the organizer).
cases.right: 2027-06-08 for the 2027 edition; the 2026 edition's dates are not on the page, so blank

cases.name: Only last year's edition exists: a start date is guessed for the next one
cases.went_wrong: Research returned START DATE 2027-05-10 and status Upcoming; the page shows the 2026 edition (Boston, April 28-30, 2026) and a 'Call for speakers' link with no date. The load wrote it back after we had cleared it.
cases.fixture: ODSC AI East. April 28-30, 2026. Menino Convention and Exhibition Center, Boston. Call for speakers.
cases.right: blank; STATUS Needs Verification until a page announces a 2027 edition

cases.name: The site blocks a plain read (anti-bot wall)
cases.went_wrong: A plain fetch returns HTTP 403 or an 84-character wall notice; early on this was mistaken for 'the quote is not on the page' and for a date-reader fault.
cases.right: unreadable by a plain fetch: report 'not checked' and read it in a browser. The browser shows: Close date: 12 October 2026 (23:59 Singapore Time GMT/UTC +8)

cases.name: Two tracks, two deadlines on one page
cases.went_wrong: Research returned the paper deadline one week and the abstract deadline the next; the customer needs one date.
cases.fixture: Important Dates. Abstract submission deadline: November 16, 2026. Research paper submission deadline: November 23, 2026. All submissions should be made electronically at https://codaspy27.hotcrp.com/
cases.right: 2026-11-16 (operator rule: the earliest is the default; both dates in the details)

cases.name: An aggregator that does not even list the event is cited as evidence
cases.went_wrong: Research cited cfptime.org ('Nov 21, 2026 at 6:59 AM PST'); the operator found the aggregator does not list the event. Our gate accepted the citation because the page was admissible and the quote was on it.
cases.fixture: CFP Time. Upcoming calls for papers: BSides Boston 2026, Hackers Next Door 2026, OWASP Global AppSec EU 2027. (The organizer of the event in question is not on this list.)
cases.right: 2026-11-20 from the organizer's own Sessionize page: Call closes at 11:59 PM 20 Nov 2026

cases.name: The same event under two names
cases.event: SAF Europe Summit 2027 / Sustainable Fuels Global Summit 2027
cases.went_wrong: Two rows with the same URL, city and start date; the old site now redirects to the new brand. Upstream's 'merge' carried no evidence.
cases.fixture: SAF Europe Summit 2027 (#SAFEU2027), taking place on 13-14 April 2027 at the Postillion Hotel & Convention Centre WTC Rotterdam.
cases.wrong: two rows, or 'Discontinued' on the old name
cases.right: one event; the retire/merge claim needs its own evidence page (R16)

checks.note: Does the method notice that two rows share URL host, city and start date, and refuse to call either dead?

cases.name: A dead domain: nothing to read, so nothing to invent
cases.went_wrong: The domain does not work. Research still returned a start date and dates text; upstream then called it 'Discontinued' with no evidence page.
cases.right: dates blank, status Needs Verification; 'discontinued' only with a page and sentence that says so (R16)

checks.note: With no page, does the method return blanks and say so?

cases.name: One brand, two different events
cases.event: Wild West Hackin' Fest (Mile High vs Deadwood)
cases.went_wrong: Different editions of one brand in different cities carry different dates; a method that matches by brand mixes them.
cases.fixture: Wild West Hackin' Fest @ Mile High 2026 (Denver) and Wild West Hackin' Fest Deadwood 2026 (Deadwood, SD) are separate events with their own dates and calls.
cases.wrong: one row, or one event's dates on the other

checks.note: Does the method keep the two events apart and give each its own dates?

cases.name: The input list's dates text is wrong; the page says otherwise
cases.went_wrong: The list said March 9-10, 2027; no page says that. The event page reads 26 - 27 January 2027 in Amsterdam.
cases.fixture: 6th European Carbon Capture, Utilization & Storage (CCUS) 2027. 26 - 27 January 2027 | Amsterdam. The conference takes place in Amsterdam.

cases.name: A two-digit-year date style
cases.went_wrong: The page writes proposal periods as '19 October (26)'; the date reader matched none of 35 occurrences until the fix.

cases.name: A claim of 2 October must not match 'October 12'
cases.went_wrong: No digit boundary: a claim of 2026-10-02 matched the page text '12 October 2026' in 5 of 5 sampled pages.

cases.name: A deadline in another time zone
cases.went_wrong: 'Nov 21, 2026 at 6:59 AM PST' is the same moment as 11:59 PM on 20 November in US Mountain time.
